speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to better understand your condition, can you describe exactly what the pain feels like and how often you are urinating?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis (Painful Bladder Syndrome).

The relieved pain upon voiding, combined with nocturia, dysuria, and pain during intercourse in a 40-year-old female, is highly characteristic of this condition. Do you have a history of similar episodes, kidney stones, or recent urinary tract infections?
